card.subject: Elapsed time is measured on the wall clock: the secrets cache keeps an expired secret across a clock step, and unit-test timing bounds fail the pre-push hook under load
card.activeForm: Moving cache expiry to a monotonic clock

origin.evidence: grep -n 'time.time()' src/lambdas/shared/secrets.py  # expiry compare and set both on the wall clock

work_items: Card #16: compute and compare cache expiry on time.monotonic() in src/lambdas/shared/secrets.py and every other cache that pairs jittered_ttl with time.time(), and make test_cache_expiry independent of real sleeps
Card #16: make the unit tests' elapsed-time upper bounds deterministic: measure on time.perf_counter() and control time or the work rather than asserting a tight wall-clock ceiling
runConfiguration.backwards_compatibility: public-contract. Every affected cache is in-process memory, so no stored expiry outlives a container. Any timestamp that is serialized, returned to a caller or compared with an external wall-clock time stays on time.time().
runConfiguration.security_tier: standard. The secrets cache is on the path; only how long a secret stays cached changes. Secret access and contents are untouched.
runConfiguration.operational_rigour: standard. Unit tests control the clock rather than sleep, and a mutant reverting each site to time.time() turns its test red. No preprod verification: nothing changed is observable there.

card.description:
MEASURED 2026-10-10 by Helios. The pre-push pytest hook failed tests/unit/test_secrets.py::TestGetSecret::test_cache_expiry (1 failed, 3652 passed, -x) on a commit that touched only cards/. In isolation the same test failed 1 run of 15.

CAUSE. _get_from_cache (src/lambdas/shared/secrets.py:311) compares time.time() against an expires_at that _set_in_cache sets as time.time() + jittered_ttl(base_ttl). time.time() is the wall clock. On this WSL2 host the wall clock is stepped repeatedly: systemd-resolved logged 'Clock change detected' about every 30 s and journald 'Time jumped backwards' several times between 13:27 and 14:03 PDT. The test sets a 1 s TTL, which jittered_ttl (src/lib/cache_utils.py:39, default 10%) stretches to as much as 1.1 s, then sleeps exactly 1.1 s. A backward step during that sleep leaves the entry unexpired, and the second get_secret returns the old value. A 1.1 s window against a ~30 s step period fits 1 failure in 15.

WHY IT IS A PRODUCT DEFECT AND NOT ONLY A TEST ONE. Expiry is an elapsed-time question; the wall clock answers it wrongly whenever the clock is adjusted. Lambda's clock is steadier than this host's, so production impact is small, but monotonic time is the correct clock for a TTL.

SCOPE. Census the other caches first: grep -rn --include='*.py' 'jittered_ttl' src/ lists every TTL site, and each one that pairs it with time.time() has the same defect. The test should control time (patch the clock or the jitter) rather than sleep at the jitter boundary.

HOST NOTE, not this card's work: why the WSL2 wall clock steps every ~30 s is a host question for the dotfiles board.

SECOND INSTANCE, MEASURED 2026-10-10 23:31 PDT by Helios. A board-only push failed the pre-push hook on tests/unit/ingestion/test_parallel_timing.py::TestParallelTiming::test_parallel_execution_with_one_source_failure (1 failed, 1091 passed, 151 s against 85 s for 3652 tests earlier the same day). The test asserts a 100 ms parallel fetch finishes under 150 ms, measured with time.time(). Load average was 27 to 30 at the time, so 50 ms of headroom is scheduler noise, and a forward clock step on this host inflates the measurement further. Census of the same shape, 8 assertions in 3 files, re-run on card-16 at 945f6c03 (tree identical to main f09ab5d5 outside cards/): grep -rn --include='*.py' -E 'assert (elapsed|duration)[a-z_]* *<' tests/unit

status.summary: The 11 jittered_ttl caches measure expiry on time.monotonic(). The secrets and OHLC expiry tests control the clock and fail when the code reads time.time(). The 8 unit-test wall-clock ceilings are gone: concurrency is proved by a barrier and events, duration_ms by fixed clock readings, CPU-bound cost by process_time(), and fails-fast by jwt.decode never being reached. make validate passes 8 of 8 blocking stages; make test-unit passes 4259 of 4259. Spec: specs/1404-monotonic-elapsed-time/spec.md.
for_the_board: Remove #16 from cards/goal.json: priority item 2 and the READY list.

Number and place cards/NEW-card-16-wall-clock-elapsed-sites.json: 36 time.time() calls left in src/ outside the caches. Some are elapsed time (SSE heartbeats, failover durations, the CloudWatch flush timer) and some are real epochs. Nothing has failed from them, so it ranks below #17 and #18. Its runConfiguration needs backwards_compatibility, security_tier and operational_rigour from the operator.
The census line in cards/16.json now cites card-16 at 945f6c03, whose tree is main f09ab5d5's outside cards/, in place of the never-pushed a2708bab.
